page: Vultr vbm-6c-128gb is a dedicated bare metal server belonging to the Bare Metal SSD family. It features an Intel Xeon 2386G processor built on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a base clock speed of 3.5 GHz. The system provides 6 physical cores and 12 virtual CPUs (vCPUs) with 2 threads per core. This dedicated CPU allocation ensures that processing resources are not shared with other tenants, delivering consistent execution times for demanding workloads.

The server is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, which translates to approximately 10.67 GB of RAM per physical core. For local storage, the configuration includes a 1920 GB solid-state drive (SSD), providing high-capacity local storage directly attached to the bare metal hardware. No graphics processing units (GPUs) are included in this configuration, as the GPU count is zero. Additionally, the server comes provisioned with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Given its bare metal architecture, the server eliminates virtualization overhead, making it highly resource-dense and cost-efficient for workloads requiring direct hardware access. The combination of a high-frequency 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon processor, 128.0 GB of RAM, and a 1920 GB SSD makes this server type suitable for memory-intensive applications, relational databases, local storage-heavy operations, and dedicated web serving environments.
